articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft just dropped 167 security fixes in one go, including a SharePoint zero-day and a Windows Defender flaw hilariously dubbed 'BlueHammer.' Nothing says 'we've got this under control' like patching 167 holes at once.

articles.title: First reports come in of victims of critical cPanel vuln as 'millions' of sites potentially exposed
articles.summary: Britain's cyber agency warns that AI is about to unleash a 'patch tsunami' by digging up decades of buried code flaws. Turns out all those technical shortcuts are finally coming home to roost, and AI is playing debt collector.

articles.title: Linux exploit instantly grants administrator access on most distributions since 2017 — cryptography optimization snafu grants root privileges to local users
articles.summary: An AI-equipped security researcher just found a nine-year-old zero-day in the Linux kernel that's been hiding in plain sight since 2017. Sometimes the best bugs are the ones that age like fine wine.

articles.title: OpenAI locks GPT-5.5-Cyber behind velvet rope despite slamming Anthropic for doing exactly that
articles.summary: Critical cPanel vulnerability is being actively exploited with 'millions' of sites potentially exposed, and at least one victim is already facing ransomware demands. When the backbone of web hosting breaks, everyone feels it.

articles.title: 30,000 Facebook Accounts Hacked via Google AppSheet Phishing Campaign
articles.summary: Cybersecurity firm Trellix got their source code stolen because irony is apparently the universe's favorite programming language. Nothing builds customer confidence like a security company that can't secure its own code.

articles.title: Polymarket Rejects Data Breach Claims as Hacker Alleges 300K Records Stolen
articles.summary: A 15-year-old hacker allegedly breached France's ID agency and tried selling millions of citizens' data on the dark web. Gen Z doesn't mess around when it comes to making pocket money.

articles.title: Digital Hopes, Real Power: From Connection to Collective Action
articles.summary: Public records laws have been exposing ALPR surveillance abuse nationwide, so naturally states want to block what the public can see. Transparency is great until it reveals how creepy the panopticon really is.

articles.title: Open Records Laws Reveal ALPRs’ Sprawling Surveillance. Now States Want to Block What the Public Sees.
articles.summary: Utah's new anti-VPN law goes into effect next week, because nothing says 'freedom' like forcing citizens to browse the internet naked. Predictably, VPN usage is already surging.

articles.title: Brace for the patch tsunami: AI is unearthing decades of buried code debt
articles.summary: The FBI redirected 9,000 personnel—a quarter of their staff—to target immigrants under Trump's deportation push, potentially compromising national security. Priorities: sorted, apparently.

articles.title: A Bridge to Somewhere: How to Link Your Mastodon, Bluesky, or Other Federated Accounts
articles.summary: Germany just doxed 'UNKN,' the elusive mastermind behind REvil and GandCrab ransomware gangs—31-year-old Russian Daniil Shchukin finally has a face to match his legendary handle. Even digital ghosts eventually get unmasked.
